source.filename: 2007-Exact static analysis of partially composite beams and beam-columns.pdf

constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic material behavior in tension and compression for all subcomponent materials (uncracked state assumed).
Linear elastic load-slip behavior for discretely located interlayer shear connectors, modeled as a continuous connection with a constant slip modulus K.
Interlayer slip is assumed small, with relative slip occurring at the interface while frictional effects and vertical uplift are neglected.
Curvature across all subcomponents in the composite cross-section is assumed identical.
Euler-Bernoulli beam theory applies to each subcomponent, neglecting shear deformation.
Axial loads are applied at the centroid of the transformed fully composite cross-section, inducing uniform axial strain without contributing directly to bending.
Uniform cross-section along the member length with continuous slope (constant bending stiffness).

Small deflections and small slopes in second-order analysis, permitting the axial load along the deformed axis to be approximated by its horizontal component and transverse load projections along the deformed axis to be neglected.
control_variables: Uniform cross-sectional dimensions and constant material properties along the beam length
Centroidal application of external axial loads F to prevent load-eccentricity-induced bending moments
Neglect of vertical separation/uplift and interface friction at the connection boundary
dependent_variables: Transverse deflection w(x) and maximum deflection w_max
Interlayer slip (Delta u) and interface slip force per unit length (Vs)
Second-order magnification factors for deflections and internal actions

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The effective bending stiffness of a partially composite beam-column varies continuously between the non-composite lower bound (EI_0) and the fully composite upper bound (EI_infinity) as a function of the interface slip modulus K, geometry, and boundary conditions via the non-dimensional composite action parameter alpha*L.

Variational energy minimization using a Lagrange multiplier to enforce strain-deflection compatibility yields the sixth-order governing differential equations and mathematically consistent, admissible boundary conditions for first- and second-order beam-column analyses.

Consistent boundary conditions for a clamped end in a partially composite member dictate that either the internal axial force must vanish (axially sliding clamped) or the interface slip must be constant/zero (axially fixed clamped), proving that intuitive assumptions of non-zero slip with zero rotation and deflection are mathematically ill-posed.

Exact buckling length coefficients for partially composite columns with interlayer slip are strictly identical to classical solid-column Euler coefficients for clamped-free (mu = 2), pinned-pinned (mu = 1), and clamped-clamped (mu = 0.5) boundary conditions.

For the clamped-pinned boundary condition (Euler case 3), the exact buckling length coefficient deviates by less than 1.8% from the classical solid-column value (0.699), and using the solid-column approximation results in a maximum deviation in buckling load of at most 2.5% on the safe side.
For two-layer composite members of rectangular cross-sections, the relative bending stiffness parameter EI_0 / EI_infinity is theoretically bounded within the range 0.25 <= EI_0 / EI_infinity < 1.

In second-order beam-column analysis, internal axial forces do not magnify uniformly like bending moments and deflections, because only the portion of the normal force induced by bending is subject to second-order magnification.

An effective bending stiffness (EI_eff) approximation predicts deflections and bending moments in partially composite members with high accuracy (errors under 3%), but produces higher errors (~15%) for interface slip and shear forces due to spatial differentiation.

future_work: Dynamic analysis of composite beams and beam-columns with partial interaction (noted as addressed in a companion paper).
Extending the formulation to handle discontinuities in flexural stiffness and slope by superimposing Macauley's singularity functions onto the one-dimensional field.
independent_variables: Boundary support conditions (Euler cases 1 through 4: clamped-free, pinned-pinned, clamped-pinned, clamped-clamped)
Transverse loading distribution and intensity q(x)
Axial compression load P or axial tension load F
Cross-sectional geometric dimensions (b1, b2, h1, h2, r1, r2, r) and constituent elastic moduli (E1, E2)
limitations_inferred: The formulation is restricted to one-dimensional kinematics and small deflections; it does not model large non-linear rotations, cross-sectional distortion, or three-dimensional out-of-plane torsional-flexural coupling.
No physical experimental testing was conducted in the paper; verification was performed solely through mathematical proofs and numerical comparisons against prior approximate formulas.
Time-dependent material effects such as viscoelastic creep, shrinkage, or relaxation are excluded from the model.
The model assumes identical curvature across sub-elements, which may break down if significant interfacial uplift or transverse normal compliance occurs.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory is adopted for individual components, neglecting shear deformation effects.
Interlayer slip is assumed small; frictional effects and vertical uplift at the interface are neglected.
Shear connectors are discrete in practice but modeled as a continuous connection with a constant linear elastic slip modulus K.
Constituent materials are restricted to linear elastic behavior in tension and compression.
The formulation assumes uniform cross-sections and continuous slopes along the member length.
The effective bending stiffness approximation is less accurate for slip forces and shear forces because they are obtained through differentiation of normal forces and moments.
main_results: Derived the sixth-order ordinary differential equations and exact general solutions for deflections and internal actions of partially composite Euler-Bernoulli beams and beam-columns under first- and second-order static loading.
Formulated mathematically consistent and well-posed boundary conditions via variational calculus, establishing that a clamped support requires either zero axial normal force or zero interface slip.

Derived exact closed-form characteristic equations and proved that the fundamental buckling length coefficients for partially composite columns are identical to those of solid columns for clamped-free (mu = 2), pinned-pinned (mu = 1), and clamped-clamped (mu = 0.5) cases.

Showed that for the clamped-pinned condition (Euler case 3), the exact buckling length coefficient differs from the solid-column value by less than 1.8% (maximum near alpha*L ~ 7), corresponding to an error in critical buckling load of at most 2.5% on the safe side.
Proved mathematically that the theoretical relative bending stiffness ratio EI_0 / EI_infinity for two-subcomponent rectangular composite members is bounded within [0.25, 1.0).
Demonstrated that second-order magnification applies only to the bending-induced component of the internal axial force, rather than the direct applied load component.

Derived a generalized effective bending stiffness expression (EI_eff) enabling accurate approximate calculations of deflections (0.4% error) and moments (2.9% error), while noting larger errors (15.1%) for differentiated shear and slip forces.
modeling_methods: Euler-Bernoulli beam kinematics applied to individual sub-elements (neglecting shear deformation)
Variational energy minimization (principle of minimum potential energy) using Lagrange multipliers to incorporate the strain-deflection constraint
Sixth-order governing ordinary differential equations for transverse deflection w(x) and internal actions under first- and second-order static loading
Continuous linear elastic interface modeling characterized by a constant slip modulus K [N/m^2]
Characteristic equation derivation, Gaussian elimination, and determinant analysis of 6x6 boundary matrices for eigenvalue and buckling length coefficient evaluation
Effective bending stiffness (EI_eff) formulation for simplified first-order and buckling approximations
performance_metrics: Magnification factor (exact second-order / first-order ratio vs approximate 1 / (1 - P/P_cr))
Percentage error / deviation of approximate methods (solid-column coefficients or EI_eff) relative to exact solutions
possible_gap_implications: The linear elastic, small-displacement beam-column formulation with interlayer slip provides a theoretical basis for layered stiffness modeling, but does not capture the large geometric deflections, hyperelastic material response, or continuous active actuation seen in soft continuum robotic systems.

The exclusion of interfacial uplift and friction limits direct application to variable stiffness mechanisms relying on friction or vacuum-driven layer jamming, where normal interface pressure and separation play a dominant role.
paper.research_objective: To rigorously derive the governing differential equations, complete general solutions, and mathematically consistent boundary conditions for partially composite Euler-Bernoulli beams and beam-columns with interlayer slip under first- and second-order static loading using variational methods; to derive exact characteristic equations and buckling length coefficients for the four Euler boundary conditions; to determine the theoretical range of the relative bending stiffness; and to formulate an effective bending stiffness for approximate deflection and internal action analyses.
paper.research_problem: Establishing mathematically consistent and well-posed boundary conditions, exact governing differential equations, and closed-form characteristic equations and buckling length coefficients for partially composite beams and beam-columns with interlayer slip under first- and second-order static axial and transverse loading.
stiffness_mechanism: shear connectors with slip modulus K
paper.title: Exact static analysis of partially composite beams and beam-columns
